# `prefer-vector-reduce`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports serial lane-by-lane arithmetic or bitwise accumulations across vector or
array lanes, recommending `@reduce`.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Chaining operations such as `v[0] + v[1] + v[2] + v[3]` extracts vector lanes
into scalar registers and executes a serial dependency chain with $N \times
\text{latency}$. The `@reduce` builtin keeps values within vector registers and
executes parallel tree reductions in $O(\log N)$ latency using hardware
reduction instructions (e.g. `haddps` or `faddp`).

## When it fires

Whenever aggregating all lanes of a vector or fixed-size array using addition,
multiplication, minimum, maximum, or bitwise operations.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn sum(v: @Vector(4, u32)) u32 {
    return v[0] + v[1] + v[2] + v[3];
}
```
